children: It was a gold-plated quarter for The Cheesecake Factory
showed a significant increase in profits thanks to cost efficiencies and a double-digit gain in revenue.

Driven by new menu additions, a popular rewards program, and increased social media exposure, the restaurant chain saw a 13.5% increase in sales to $1.03B and a 15.2% increase in comparable sales, both of which beat expectations of $1.0B and 9.53%, respectively.

“We delivered an exceptional third quarter, generating record quarterly revenue, with margins and earnings also exceeding our expectations,” said David Overton, The Cheesecake Factory’s chairman and CEO. “The Cheesecake Factory restaurants led our performance, with comparable sales and traffic meaningfully outperforming the broader casual dining industry.”

Improvements in food efficiency and labor productivity bolstered profits by 50% to $1.02 per share, 6 cents better than expected. This was reflected in modest gains in food and beverage costs and labor expenses, both of which were a smaller percentage of sales compared to the same quarter last year.

During the quarter, the company opened six new restaurants, including two Cheesecake Factory restaurants, one North Italia, one Flower Child, and two Fox Restaurant Concepts. In FY26, the company plans to open 26 new restaurants.

title: From gaudy to golden: The Cheesecake Factory serves up a well-timed beat
